Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of Iowa|Governor]] [[Terry Branstad]] did not seek re-election to a fifth consecutive term; he later successfully ran again in [[2010 Iowa gubernatorial election|2010]] and [[2014 Iowa gubernatorial election|2014]]. To replace him, [[Iowa State Senate|State Senator]] [[Tom Vilsack]] narrowly won the nomination of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] while former [[United States Congressman]] [[Jim Ross Lightfoot]], who was previously the Republican nominee for the [[United States Senate]] in [[1996 United States Senate election in Iowa|1996]], won his party's nomination. Lightfoot was the odds-on favorite to win and polling consistently showed him in the lead,{{Cite web |url=http://www.news-releases.uiowa.edu/1998/november/1102heartland.html |title = Despite tight race for Iowa governor, Lightfoot ahead among most likely voters |access-date=2014-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901153622/http://www.news-releases.uiowa.edu/1998/november/1102heartland.html |archive-date=2006-09-01 |url-status=dead }} but Vilsack won the general election in a stunning upset, becoming the first Democrat to serve as governor of Iowa since 1969 and the 5th Democrat to hold the office in the 20th century. Lightfoot never [[Concession (politics)|conceded]] defeat.{{cite web |authorlink=O. Kay Henderson|last=Henderson |first=O.
